toc.title: When Your Request Conflicts with Policy

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. AI: artificial intelligence

  • What an organizational AI policy contains and how to follow it
  • Governance roles and controls: owners, approvals, logging, review
  • The ethical issues in everyday AI use: honesty, fairness, privacy, accountability, transparency
  • How to act when a request conflicts with policy or ethics

2Organizational AI Policies

Running case

Cedarbrook's AI Use Policy

  • After a pilot, Cedarbrook publishes a one-page AI use policy: approved tools and accounts, data rules, what must be reviewed, how to disclose AI use, who to ask
  • A new analyst wants to use a free tool they found online; the policy says to use only the approved Claude workspace

An AI policy turns principles into rules for daily work. Typical parts:

Policy part What it says Your duty
Approved tools and accounts Which AI tools, plans and workspaces may be used Use only those; no personal accounts for company data
Data rules What data may enter AI tools (Module 13) Classify, minimize, anonymize
Allowed and prohibited uses Examples of each Check before starting a new kind of use
Review requirements When a person must check outputs, and who Follow the review steps; keep a record
Disclosure When to tell customers, colleagues or regulators that AI was used Disclose as required
Intellectual property Ownership and use of AI outputs and of third-party material Do not paste others' confidential or copyrighted material improperly
Training and access Who may use which features (connectors, Skills, file creation) Complete training; respect feature limits
Incident reporting What to do when something goes wrong (data leak, harmful output) Report quickly to the named contact
  • Policy first. Product features and settings do not override your organization's rules. If the policy and a tool's capability differ, follow the policy.
  • Admins control what is available: on Team and Enterprise plans owners can enable or restrict web search, connectors, Skills, file creation, sharing and memory.
  • When the policy does not cover your case, ask the policy owner before proceeding.
Exam tip

In policy scenarios, the correct choice usually follows the written policy and approved tools, asks the policy owner when it is silent, and reports incidents promptly.

3Governance in Practice

Governance is the set of roles, rules and checks that keep AI use safe, lawful and valuable.

Element Example at Cedarbrook
Ownership Each Project, Skill and shared prompt has a named owner
Approval New use cases and connectors are approved before rollout
Risk tiers Low (internal drafts), medium (customer-facing text), high (decisions about people, regulated content) with matching review
Human oversight A qualified person reviews outputs in medium and high tiers
Records Log of high-risk uses, reviewers and decisions
Quality checks Sample reviews of outputs; tracked error rate
Training Short course for all users, with examples
Change control Instructions and knowledge updated by the owner, tested and logged (Module 12)
Incident response Defined steps for data leaks or harmful output
Review cycle Policy revisited as tools and laws change

  • Accountability stays with people. An AI cannot be held responsible; the person who uses or approves the output is.
  • Proportionate controls. More review for higher risk; avoid heavy process on low-risk tasks.

4Ethics of Everyday AI Use

Principle Meaning Examples
Honesty and transparency Do not mislead people about AI involvement or about what the output is Disclose AI-assisted content when required; do not present invented sources as real; do not impersonate
Fairness Avoid unfair treatment and bias Review hiring, grading and customer-service outputs for bias; do not let Claude make people decisions alone
Privacy Respect the people behind the data Minimize, anonymize, follow consent
Accountability A named person owns the result Review before sending; keep records
Safety and non-harm Avoid content or actions that could hurt people Do not use Claude to deceive, harass or defraud
Respect for creators Do not misuse others' work Check copyright and licensing; cite sources
Human dignity and judgment Keep people in control of decisions about people Human review for high-stakes cases
Reliability Do not overstate what AI can do Communicate limits; verify

Common dilemmas

  • Passing off AI work as purely your own where disclosure is expected (school, publication, client work with a disclosure clause)

  • Using AI-generated reviews, testimonials or fake personas to influence customers (deceptive, prohibited)

  • Automating a decision about a person (hiring, credit, discipline) without human review

  • Feeding an employee's or customer's private information into a tool without a legitimate basis

  • Generating realistic content that could mislead (fake quotes, edited images presented as real)

  • Over-trusting outputs in safety, medical or legal contexts

  • Anthropic's Usage Policy requires disclosure to affected people in high-risk uses and expects consumer-facing chatbots to say they are AI.

  • Claude's output may carry marks (invisible text watermarks and content credentials for files) so provenance can sometimes be checked; absence of a mark proves nothing.

  • The Associate does not need to resolve every ethical question alone: spot the issue, apply the policy and escalate (to a manager, Legal, Privacy or an ethics contact).

Exam tip

Ethical-scenario answers favor transparency, fairness checks, human accountability and privacy. Options that hide AI use, skip review of people decisions or fabricate content are wrong.

5When Your Request Conflicts with Policy

  1. Stop before sharing data or sending output.
  2. Check the policy and the data class.
  3. Choose a compliant path: remove sensitive data, use the approved tool, add human review, or change the task.
  4. Ask the policy owner, Legal or Privacy if still unsure.
  5. Report any breach or near miss at once.
  6. Record the decision.
Exam tip

Policy first, then people: follow the approved tools and rules, ask the owner when the policy is silent, and report incidents quickly.

6Exam Q&A

S1A new analyst wants to use a free AI website they found instead of the company's approved Claude workspace. What should they do?

  • AUse both and compare
  • BUse the free site, because AI tools are all alike and the company will not notice
  • CAsk the free site's own terms of service for permission to use company data
  • DUse only the approved workspace, per the AI policy
Show the answer

Answer: D. Approved tools and accounts are a core policy requirement.

S2An employee notices that a chat shared earlier included a customer's phone number. What is the best next step?

  • AUnshare the chat and report the incident to the named contact under the policy
  • BWait to see whether anyone notices before deciding whether it is worth reporting at all
  • CIgnore it
  • DDelete their account only
Show the answer

Answer: A. The right response is to contain the exposure by unsharing the chat and then report the incident promptly to the named contact.

S3A marketer wants Claude to create customer testimonials with invented names to post on the website. What is the correct response?

  • ADo it but add a tiny disclaimer saying that the testimonials were written by Claude
  • BAsk Claude for more testimonials
  • CDecline; fabricated testimonials are deceptive and violate the usage policy
  • DDo it, because testimonials are marketing and marketing text does not need to be real
Show the answer

Answer: C. Fake reviews and personas are prohibited deceptive activity.

S4Which statement about accountability is correct?

  • AThe people who use and approve AI output are accountable for it
  • BThe AI is responsible for its output
  • CNobody is responsible
  • DOnly IT is responsible
Show the answer

Answer: A. An AI system cannot be held responsible, so accountability stays with the people who use, review and approve its output.

S5The AI policy does not mention using Claude to summarize supplier contracts. What should the employee do?

  • AProceed, because it is not prohibited anywhere in the written policy
  • BAsk Claude whether it is allowed
  • CAsk the policy owner or Legal before proceeding
  • DUse a personal account
Show the answer

Answer: C. When policy is silent on a sensitive use, ask first.

S6Which TWO are ethical practices when using Claude to help screen job applications? Select TWO.

  • ATelling applicants when AI is part of the process where required
  • BUsing whatever data is available, including private social posts
  • CHiding AI use to avoid questions
  • DLetting Claude reject candidates without review
  • EReviewing outputs for bias and keeping a qualified person deciding
Show the answer

Answer: A, E. Reviewing outputs for bias, keeping a qualified person as the decision-maker and being open about AI use are the fair and transparent practices.

S7A manager wants to present AI-drafted analysis as verified fact without checking it. What principle is breached?

  • APrivacy only, because the manager did not share any personal data with Claude
  • BFairness only, because the manager did not treat any group of people unfairly
  • CNone
  • DReliability and honesty: outputs must be checked and not overstated
Show the answer

Answer: D. Presenting unchecked output as verified fact overstates reliability, misleads readers and skips the verification that responsible use requires.

S8Which control best fits a high-risk use such as decisions about benefits?

  • AA longer prompt
  • BReview only on complaint
  • CNo review
  • DQualified human review, records, and disclosure to the affected people
Show the answer

Answer: D. High-risk uses require human oversight, accountability and transparency.

S9An employee finds that Claude produced text closely matching a copyrighted article. What is the best action?

  • APublish it
  • BCheck the source, avoid copying protected material, and follow IP policy
  • CRemove the author's name
  • DAsk Claude to reword it slightly and publish
Show the answer

Answer: B. Respect creators' rights; verify originality and follow policy.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Policy first Features do not override the organization's rules
Policy parts Approved tools · data · allowed uses · review · disclosure · IP · training · incidents
When silent Ask the policy owner, Legal or Privacy
Governance Owners · approvals · risk tiers · human oversight · records · training · incident response
Accountability People, not the AI
Ethics Honesty · fairness · privacy · accountability · safety · respect for creators · human judgment · reliability
Red flags Fake reviews or personas · automated people decisions · hiding AI use · private data without basis
High-risk uses Qualified human review plus disclosure
Incident Contain, report, record
